description: Copper is a chemical element with symbol Cu and atomic number 29. It is a soft, malleable, and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity, and a freshly exposed surface of pure copper has a pinkish-orange color.
uses: Copper is used as a conductor of heat and electricity, as a building material, and as a constituent of various metal alloys such as sterling silver, cupronickel, and constantan. It is also used in decorative art, as bacteriostatic agents, fungicides, and wood preservatives, and serves essential functions in aerobic organisms particularly in oxygen metabolism.
characteristics: Copper has high electrical conductivity of 59.6×106 S/m and the second highest thermal conductivity among pure metals at room temperature. When exposed to air, it slowly oxidizes to form a protective layer of brown-black copper oxide, and can develop a green patina called verdigris on structures. It does not react with water but tarnishes when exposed to sulfur compounds.
